newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: High Asia diesel price opens western arbitrage.
newsitem.headline: High Asia diesel price opens western arbitrage.

text.p: Strong regional demand has kept Singapore diesel prices steady in the face of recent steep falls in the west and traders are exploring opportunities of moving in western cargoes, industry sources said on Thursday.

Demand from Indonesia, India, Japan and China has kept prompt physical prices above the $30.00-per-barrel mark. On Wednesday, diesel was assessed at $30.30 per barrel free-on-board (fob) Singapore basis.

At the same time, November swaps in Singapore also held its ground, trading to a high of 30.70 on Monday. November swaps were last quoted at $30.60/30.70 on Thursday up 40 cents from Wednesday, brokers said.

On the other hand, November gas oil (diesel) futures on London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) slumped to $217.25 per tonne on Wednesday from its five-year peak of around $247.00 in early October.

As a result of the sharp IPE decline, the east-west price relationship reversed back in favour of the east and has opened the possibility of exports to Asia from the Middle East, Mediterrenean and even the US West Coast, traders said.
The east-west spread was at $20.50 per tonne in favour of the west in early October but this has reversed to $10.35 in favour of the east on Thursday.
"The US West Coast is beginning to look interesting for gas oil right now due to the high distillate stocks there," one trader said.

Others said that one cargo from the Mediterrenean might also head eastwards due to its higher sulphur content of between 0.2 to 0.3 percent which cannot meet the new European specifications of 0.05 percent sulphur.

Prices in the west slumped following the release on Tuesday of stock data by the American Petroleum Institute (API) which showed a total distillate stock build of 3.6 million barrels for the week ended October 25.
The market was expecting a 1.9-million barrel stock build.
Heating oil stocks gained 1.6 million barrels with distillate production in the US at a record 3.8 million barrels per day.
Traders in Singapore said they expect IPE gas oil to undergo a technical rebound but they believe that the rise would not take prices back to their five-year highs.
The Singapore gas oil market in Singapore was boosted by an almost doubling of Indonesia's purchases for November barrels which many players estimate at between four and five million barrels.
"There are rumors in the market that Indonesia is seeking another million barrels for November and this is keeping prices firm," one trader said.
Other traders added that prices were also supported by India's decision to buy 520,000-tonnes in December, up from an initial expectation of around 300,000-tonnes.
Demand also picked up from China due to low stock levels, traders said. A 30,000-tonne cargo was sold on Wednesday at $238 per tonne cost-and-freight South China, one source said.
South Korean diesel supplies have also almost dried up due purchases by the Japanese for early December arrival, traders said.
